item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable evidence that Sisi openly admitted failure or made a broad domestic political opening in response to pressure. The strongest positive signals are mostly selective and tactical: IMF-backed macro correction, cabinet/security reshuffles, Gaza mediation, and limited detention/civil-society easing. The evidence for domestic repression, however, remains broad and contemporaneous, so the best reading is regime-preserving adaptation, not deep institutional correction.","evidence":[{"title":"IMF Executive Board Completes the First and Second Reviews of Egypt’s EFF","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-03-29","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/29/pr24101-egypt-imf-executive-board-completes-first-second-reviews-eff-approves-augmentation","summary":"Egypt was correcting policy slippages through a flexible exchange rate, tighter monetary/fiscal policy, reduced public investment, and a more level playing field for the private sector. This shows crisis management through coercion, not responsive correction.","question_ids":["8B.9","8B.8","8B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-29","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"Authorities renewed prosecutions of critics and journalists, including cases tied to corruption reporting involving senior pro-Sisi figures.
